Inverse-response atlas: proposal map + checked designs

A fast starting-point map for the four target gaps. The PWE and COMSOL layers remain separate. Smooth contours are interpolation—not accepted families of designs.

4/4 new cases passed the unchanged acceptance checks.

Left markers: small white dots = 58 M20 samples; white rings = 12 earlier accepted M25 cases; × = new atlas starts; green diamonds = new accepted M25 cases; red diamonds = new unsuccessful cases. Overlapping markers may hide individual cases. Right dots = the 64 processed COMSOL designs; the background between them is bilinear interpolation.

The M20 proposal surface is frozen at atlas v2; new validation points are not refitted into it. Hover over a marker for its recorded gap. Both panels share the color scale but retain their actual, slightly different physical axis bounds.

How much should we trust the contours?

At 49 common supported COMSOL coordinates, the PWE interpolation/reference gap difference has MAE 0.197 GHz and maximum 0.800 GHz. This combines interpolation and physical-model differences; it is not pure solver error.

Use contours to propose a geometry, then run full-path M20 and unchanged-geometry M25. No contour-wide 0.05 GHz guarantee is claimed. A negative signed gap means band overlap.

No full-Brillouin-zone, continuum, unique-inverse or fabrication-robustness certificate. Detailed report · Audited data and provenance
